plan.title: Liver 3-group DESeq2 LRT + pairwise contrasts + GSEA
plan.analytical_narrative: 12 human liver bulk RNA-seq samples (salmon gene counts, 12000 genes x 12 samples) span three unpaired groups of 4 (control, treated_a, treated_b), single batch. Two questions are asked: (1) which genes differ across all three groups at all — answered by a DESeq2 likelihood ratio test of the full model ~condition against the reduced model ~1, which is the correct any-difference test because 'condition' spans two coefficients and a single Wald test cannot answer it; and (2) which genes each treatment changes relative to control — answered by two named pairwise Wald contrasts (treated_a vs control, treated_b vs control) with control set as the explicit reference level. QC precedes modeling (blind VST, PCA, sample-distance heatmap, library sizes) to confirm the three groups separate and no sample is an outlier before any test is trusted. Independent low-count filtering and DESeq2's internal median-of-ratios normalization precede the tests; ashr shrinks each pairwise log2 fold change since a two-level contrast is not a single model coefficient (apeglm's domain). BH-FDR at alpha 0.05 with independent filtering is applied within each contrast (LRT and each pairwise Wald) separately, and each gene table reports both the shrunken and unshrunken log2FC. Each contrast's full ranked gene list (Wald/LRT statistic) is then tested against MSigDB Hallmark and Reactome human gene sets with fgsea, since an ORA on a short significant list has no power when the list is uncertain to exceed ~50 genes at this sample size (4/group). A final report step consolidates DE tables, fit diagnostics (MA plot, dispersion plot, p-value histograms), enrichment tables with leading-edge genes, and a full reproducibility record (session info, seed, package and gene-set-collection versions).

fgsea preranked GSEA on Wald statistic, Hallmark then Reactome, per contrast
Combined DE + enrichment report with diagnostics and reproducibility record
